methods.label: Use the common x-intercept
methods.explanation:
At an \(x\)-intercept, \(y=0\). Since \(a\) is positive, the two lines have respective \(x\)-intercepts
\[
x=-\frac5a\qquad\text{and}\qquad x=-\frac b3.
\]
Equating these gives \(15=ab\). The integer restrictions now reduce the problem to finding positive factor pairs of \(15\):
\[
(a,b)=(1,15),(3,5),(5,3),(15,1).
\]
These are all the possibilities, since the positive divisors of \(15\) are \(1,3,5,15\), and each determines \(b=15/a\). The pair \((3,5)\) is included even though the two equations then describe the same line; they still have the same \(x\)-intercept.

The corresponding coordinates are distinct and equal to
\[
-5,\quad-\frac53,\quad-1,\quad-\frac13.
\]
Their sum is
\[
-5-\frac53-1-\frac13=-6-2=\boxed{-8},
\]
choice E.
